ov: A small rattlesnake of the deserts of the southwestern US and northwestern Mexico. It moves by sidewinding, which leaves J-shaped tracks in loose sand, and has horn-like scales over its eyes. Females are larger than males, which is unique among US rattlesnakes.
rg: Deserts of California, Nevada, Utah and Arizona, and Sonora and Baja California in Mexico.
df: Adults eat mainly desert rodents, birds and other snakes; young ones lure lizards by wiggling their tails.
fx: Sidewinding lets it climb sand slopes as steep as the sand can hold without slipping.
The AIM-9 Sidewinder missile is named after it: both track targets by infrared.
